steps:
mfetchy - download music from YouTube Music, Apple Music, Spotify, Tidal, Deezer,
SoundCloud, Bandcamp, Qobuz/Amazon through Lucida, and direct file links

  mfy                     open mfetchy: downloads, your library, settings and tools in one place
  mfy <link or file>...   download right away: YouTube, Apple Music, Spotify, Tidal, Deezer,
                          SoundCloud, Bandcamp, Qobuz or Amazon Music links (songs, albums,
                          playlists), a direct file link, a Takeout .zip, folder or .csv, or a
                          text file of links. Songs come from YouTube (the fastest); Apple
                          Music, Tidal and the others give what YouTube can't, and the songs
                          of a link from them. Settings > Download from changes it.

Options for one run (your defaults are in mfetchy's Settings):
  -o DIR       music folder          -f FORMAT   mp3, m4a, opus, flac
  --no-vpn     skip the VPN this run -j N        max parallel downloads
  --connections N   VPN exits to use this run
  --dry-run    show what would happen, download nothing
  --retry=false  leave out the songs that were unavailable before (they are tried
               again unless Settings > Retry unavailable is off)
  --song       just the songs given: a song link normally brings its whole album, and a
               playlist or library the rest of every album it has a song from
               (--albums=false turns that off too; --albums-min N: only albums with N
               or more of your songs; the default is in Settings)
  --source youtube  YouTube only: no Apple Music, Tidal, Deezer or Lucida at all
  --source best     look every song up on Apple Music, Tidal and Deezer first (best quality)
                    (--maybe: also take less certain Apple matches)
  --premium-upgrade   re-download songs at YouTube Premium quality (experimental,
                      slow, uses your account: turn it on in Settings first)
  -y           assume yes
  --completion SHELL  print tab completion for bash, zsh, fish or powershell
  --version, --help
